forecast-period.text: A high pressure system briefly establishes in the north today. Another series of troughs and cold fronts are expected to enter western SA early on Sunday, crossing the state and then clearing in the east by the end of Monday. A ridge of high pressure will then push into western SA on Monday before the associated high moves into waters south on Tuesday. A trough over the WA/NT border will also extend into SA at times from Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural areas, mostly clearing by the afternoon. Isolated thunderstorms possible across the far northeast. Maximum temperatures below average, tending near average in the west. Light and variable winds in the north, tending northwest to southwesterly winds across the south.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing across the north and west, becoming scattered and extending into central and eastern districts during the late afternoon and evening. Severe thunderstorms are possible, bringing damaging wind gusts about parts of the pastoral districts extending into the Eyre Peninsula. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh at times in the north, as a south to southwesterly change moves into the far west during the afternoon.

Scattered showers and thunderstorms across central and eastern districts during the morning and afternoon, tending isolated in the west. Thunderstorms contract to the north in the late afternoon and possibly tend severe with a damaging wind gust risk in the northeast. Maximum temperatures below average in the east, grading to well below average in the west. North to northwesterly winds in the far north, ahead of moderate south to southwesterly change extending throughout and freshening near the coast.

text.p: Isolated light showers possible about the southern agricultural area and isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms about the north, more likely in the northwest. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times in the northeast and tending southwest to southerly about the southern agricultural area.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: Broadly 2 to 10 mm across the pastoral districts, with isolated falls reaching 10-20 mm. 5-15 mm about the agricultural areas, with isolated higher falls of 15-25 mm possible. Localised falls of up to 40 mm are possible with severe thunderstorms.
